approved: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
The bill would change when certain visa decisions are considered to have been made.
It would clarify the rules for submitting another protection visa application after a refusal.
It would add a requirement that a protection visa applicant must not be found to be a security risk by the Australian Security Intelligence Organisation.
Specify that a visa decision is taken to be made when a record is created, not when it is told to the person.
Clarify how the bar on making a further protection visa application operates.
Make it a condition for granting a protection visa that the applicant is not assessed as a risk to security by ASIO.
Visa applicants, review applicants, former visa holders, and the Minister or his delegate.

Introduced a bill amending the Migration Act in response to recent Federal Court and High Court rulings, clarifying when a visa decision is finally determined, restoring a bar on repeat protection visa applications on different grounds, and reinstating a criterion requiring applicants not be assessed by ASIO as a security risk.

The Selection of Bills Committee presented its 11th report of 2013, recommending six bills be referred to specific committees for inquiry with set reporting dates, including the Environment Legislation Amendment Bill 2013 (report by 12 February 2014) and the Criminal Code Amendment (Harming Australians) Bill 2013 (report by 4 March 2014).

Announced Labor's support for the Migration Amendment Bill 2013, which clarifies when a protection visa decision is finally made, bars repeat applications on new grounds after a failed claim, and blocks a protection visa for anyone with a negative ASIO security assessment, while noting the Stone review process remains intact.

Announced Labor's support for the Migration Amendment Bill 2013, citing the Federal Court's 2012 SZQOY decision and its 11 September 2013 SZRNY judgement on when a protection visa review decision becomes final, and the SZGIZ case on repeat applications.

Opposed the Migration Amendment Bill 2013 on behalf of the Greens, arguing it denies refugees the right to know or challenge adverse ASIO security assessments, and cited a UN Human Rights Committee finding that Australia committed 143 human rights violations by indefinitely detaining 46 refugees, including children.

Summed up the Migration Amendment Bill 2013 as the responsible minister, describing schedules that clarify when protection visa decisions are finalised, close a loophole allowing repeat applications identified in the SZGIZ Federal Court case, and address the High Court's M47/2012 ruling on ASIO security assessments, noting the department employs over 10,000 staff.
